This is not the bare prime-value feedback or independent totient key already tested. The extra stream prevents the ciphertext difference from simply exposing shifted plaintext, while nonlinear feedback may dilute the totient stream's residual structure. Decryption remains causal given the stream alignment and rejection path. The estimated 87 doublets assumes approximately uniform candidate ciphertext; the other three statistics still require simulation. The listed constant-affine sweeps and additive position-key sweeps do not establish coverage of this changing coefficient combined with totient skip-on-repeat. Every coefficient is invertible, so a published clock and alignment suffice for ordinary keyed decoding with rejection-path search. It changes both ingredients responsible for the failed bare plaintext autokeys: feedback is nonlinear, and it is not the entire key. The explicit novelty against the supplied ledger is composite prime-value plaintext feedback plus a totient base under soft ciphertext rejection, rather than another seed or sign of a bare autokey. It remains causally decryptable after initialization, although rejection creates alignment ambiguity. Unlike the additive chains and sample bijections listed in the ledger, this proposal adds a changing totient base and applies soft rejection. A bijection preserves a uniform input distribution, making flat marginals more plausible than for a many-to-one prime-value map, although temporal structure still needs testing. The gap distribution alone is strongly nonuniform, so a plain additive gap key would be a poor candidate. raw.instructions: You are a cryptanalyst on a panel attacking the unsolved pages of Cicada 3301's Liber Primus. You propose cipher constructions; a computational gate simulates each one and rejects any that does not reproduce the pages' four statistics. You never write code. Every construction must be assembled from the menu you are given, in the JSON schema you are given, and nothing else. Think about what the author demonstrably did and about why the surviving construction (a key re-drawn when it would repeat the previous rune) has that statistical shape, then propose the mechanisms most likely to be the real one, ranked, each with a one-paragraph rationale tied to the book's own methods and hints. Do not re-propose families the brief lists as already swept under the same repeat rule unless you change something the ledgers did not try, and say what.
